column8: The public label router passes a cloned caller alias slice to TJ's labelrouting.Table under its existing mutex. The table keeps release normalization and selection; later caller slice mutation cannot replace the bound routing configuration.
The constructor creates a new labelrouting.Table with no caller containers. Subsequent configuration enters through the cloned setter; RouteQuery and RouteWrite consume that same table.

Composite label routing clones the alias slice before the retained shared Table.Set call while holding c.mu. The caller cannot alter future constituent selection by retaining and editing its input slice.

Before constructing the composite, maps.Clone detaches constituents, backing names and access modes. Defaults derive from the owned mode map, while each Engine value remains the exact issued provider; no deep copy substitutes its live data view.

Statement-view issuance clones constituent/name/mode maps and the label-route map while holding the composite read lock. Alias slices are immutable owned entries after SetLabelRouting; later setters replace an entry rather than mutate its slice, so shallow map copying retains a fixed configuration without copying graph data. Nested property routing already clones its maps.
QueryAnalyzer hands a cloned alias slice to the maintainer's normalized routing table. Query analysis uses the same table, so caller container edits cannot retarget the binding.

QueryAnalyzer allocates its table and property/default maps itself. This constructor accepts no external containers; later label configuration uses its cloned handoff, preserving one normalization owner.
